beats.say: Scammers open fake pages and channels in the name of ministries and officials.
Look at the address, not the name: an extra letter, word or number gives a fake away.
A fake account rushes you and asks for money, card details or a click.
When in doubt, open the organisation's website yourself and check its list of official accounts.

scenes.title: Messages in an official name
scenes.intro: Messages arrive on your phone in a ministry's name. Choose the right step for each.

body.text: Dear citizen! Every family is granted a one-off state payment of 300 AZN.
To receive it, enter your card details today:

steps.say: The channel name looks official. But where does the link go?

actions.label: Open link
actions.feedback: This page steals card details. A ministry does not ask for your full card details by message to pay aid.

actions.label: Report channel
actions.feedback: Right. The address is not the ministry's site, and a report gets the channel closed faster.

actions.label: Block
actions.feedback: Good, the channel cannot reach you again. Report it too so others are protected.

actions.label: Send to family group
actions.feedback: Sharing an unchecked message sends your family into the trap too. Check the official site first.

messages.text: Your application 2026-118 has been received. You can see its status in your personal account on sxn.example.

steps.say: Last week you sent an application to the ministry.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. It matches the application you made, has no link and asks for nothing.

actions.label: Report
actions.feedback: Caution is fine, but this one is genuine: it asks for nothing and lets you open the site yourself.

body.text: Hello. This is my new number. I'm in a meeting and can't call.
Send me a copy of this morning's official letter here, urgently.

steps.say: A familiar title, but a number you do not know.

actions.label: Send the letter
actions.feedback: An official document went to an unknown number. Scammers often write in a manager's name like this.

actions.label: Call the manager's known number
actions.feedback: Well done. Always check a new number through a channel you already know.

actions.label: Report and block
actions.feedback: Right. Tell security as well: colleagues may get the same message.

actions.label: Who is this?
actions.feedback: Replying keeps the chat going, and the scammer has a convincing answer ready. Check by phone.

steps.label: Ministry of Social Services: 1000 free laptops! Sign-up fee 5 AZN

actions.label: Take part
actions.feedback: A state body never charges a fee for a prize. This fake page collects card details.

actions.label: Report page
actions.feedback: Right. The extra word in the address gives it away, and a report gets it removed.

actions.label: Check on the ministry's site
actions.feedback: Great habit. If the site has no such contest, report the page.

scenes.prompt: Tap the signs of a fake channel.

body.text: Comments are closed, no questions please.

spots.label: Handle
spots.explain: The official handle is @sxn_resmi. One letter has been changed here.

spots.label: Rush
spots.explain: Scammers rush you so you have no time to think.

spots.label: Fee request
spots.explain: You never have to pay to receive a state payment.

spots.label: Link
spots.explain: The domain is not the ministry's sxn.example.

spots.label: Closed comments
spots.explain: Closing comments silences people who would warn others.

cards.explain: This is the ministry's own site. Take the list of official accounts from a page like this.
The extra word at the end is a typical sign of a fake. The official address is sxn.resmi.

body.text: Booking a job interview costs 20 AZN. Your place is held after payment.

cards.explain: A state body does not ask for money by message for an interview or application.

body.text: Reception hours have changed. Details on sxn.example.

cards.explain: It asks for nothing and points to the official site. Still confirm details on the site itself.

scenes.prompt: How do you check an account is official? Put the steps in order.

items.label: Type the organisation's website into the browser yourself
Find the links to its official accounts on the site
Compare the account address letter by letter
If it does not match, report the account to the platform

scenes.explain: Always start the check from the organisation's own site, never from a link in the message.

question.prompt: The account has a verification badge next to its name. Does that prove it is official?

options.label: Yes, the badge is a guarantee
options.feedback: On some platforms a badge can be bought, and fakes also put a badge symbol inside the name.

options.label: Yes, if it has many followers
options.feedback: Followers can be bought, and an old page can simply be renamed.

options.label: No, I check it against the link on the organisation's site
options.feedback: Right. The link on the organisation's own site is the most reliable check.

scenes.explain: Badges, followers and a neat logo can be faked. The organisation's own site cannot.

points: Check the account address, not the name: one letter can differ.
Official bodies do not ask for card details, fees or urgent payments by message.
When in doubt, open the site yourself and report the fake account.
